Technical details
  • Every 15 minutes: the shop's A record points at our server, and HTTPS answers with a valid certificate.
  • Daily: the same, plus MX, SPF, DKIM and DMARC records, a comparison of the DNS records against the backup taken at launch, and a test order with a fresh code through the public form (proof: form POST accepted, SMTP accepted; IMAP or the owner's tap for delivery).
  • Failures are re-checked after 60 seconds. The Doctor (Claude) only chooses from a fixed playbook in code: re-point the A record, re-add MX, re-add SPF/DKIM/DMARC, retry the certificate, or restore the DNS backup. """S12: the interactive landing sections may only say what the code does. Every "If it breaks here" sentence, fix and play-through step is pinned here to the checker, the playbook, the Doctor's code-written steps and the monitor.""" import re from pathlib import Path import pytest from app import incidents from app.agents import checker, investigator from app.agents.playbook import fixes_for from app.monitor import scheduler SRC = (Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "frontend" / "src" / "LandingProof.tsx").read_text(encoding="utf-8") CHECKER = Path(checker.__file__).read_text(encoding="utf-8") HOP_CHECK = {"Address": "site_points", "Secure page": "https", "Your shop": "https", "Order form": "test_order", "Mail server": "test_order", "Your inbox": "test_order"} def hops() -> list[dict]: block = SRC.split("export const HOP_INFO", 1)[1].split("];", 1)[0] out = [] for chunk in block.split(" name: ")[1:]: def field(k: str, chunk=chunk) -> str | None: m = re.search(rf'\b{k}:\s*"((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"', chunk) return m.group(1) if m else None out.append({"name": chunk.split('"')[1], "see": field("see"), "fix": field("fix"), "doctor": field("doctor"), "needs": "needsYou: true" in chunk}) return out def test_six_hops_in_the_order_the_checker_proves_them(): assert [h["name"] for h in hops()] == list(HOP_CHECK) @pytest.mark.parametrize("hop", hops(), ids=lambda h: h["name"]) def test_each_hop_breaks_with_the_real_words_and_the_real_fix(hop): check = HOP_CHECK[hop["name"]] assert f'"{hop["see"]}"' in CHECKER # the checker's own sentence for this failure if hop["fix"]: assert not hop["needs"] assert hop["fix"] in fixes_for(check, "sandbox") # a fix the playbook really allows on a shop like this assert hop["doctor"] == incidents.FIX_WORDS[hop["fix"]] else: assert hop["needs"] and not fixes_for(check, "sandbox") # the exact steps the code writes for this failure (or the opening of them) written = investigator.next_step(check, "sandbox", hop["see"]) if "mail server" in hop["name"].lower(): written = investigator.MAIL_SIGN_IN_REFUSED assert written.startswith(hop["doctor"].replace("“", "“").replace("”", "”")), hop["name"] def test_the_inbox_hop_is_proven_only_by_the_owner(): assert "Proven when you tap “Yes, I got it”" in SRC and "proven when you tap" in SRC def test_examples_are_labelled(): assert SRC.count("Example") >= 3 def test_watch_day_matches_the_monitor(): assert scheduler.QUICK_MINUTES == 15 and "const TICKS = 96" in SRC # 24 h / 15 min assert scheduler.RECHECK_SECONDS == 60 and "We check again a minute later" in SRC assert scheduler.QUICK_CHECKS == ["site_points", "https"] assert "your address still leads to your shop, and it opens securely" in SRC steps = SRC.split("export const BREAK_STEPS", 1)[1].split("];", 1)[0] assert "Looked up where your address leads → it leads nowhere" in steps assert incidents.FIX_WORDS["repoint_site"] in steps and "Checked again: working" in steps # an email only for what is still broken after the fix, once per problem (scheduler.check_alert) assert "No email this time" in steps and "one email about it, and no more about that problem" in steps """S10.5b copy rule: the landing page may only claim what the code does. Its schedule numbers are pinned here to the monitor and renewal constants, so changing one without the other fails.""" from pathlib import Path from app import renewals from app.monitor import scheduler LANDING = (Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "frontend" / "src" / "Landing.tsx").read_text(encoding="utf-8") def test_quick_check_interval(): assert scheduler.QUICK_MINUTES == 15 and "Every 15 minutes" in LANDING assert scheduler.QUICK_CHECKS == ["site_points", "https"] def test_daily_checks_cover_what_the_page_says(): daily = scheduler.daily_checks("sandbox") for name in ("site_points", "https", "email_mx", "email_spf", "email_dkim", "email_dmarc", "settings_match", "test_order"): assert name in daily assert "Every day" in LANDING and "a real test order goes through your order form" in LANDING def test_recheck_and_alert_wording(): assert scheduler.RECHECK_SECONDS == 60 and "We check again a minute later" in LANDING assert "once about that problem" in LANDING def test_renewal_thresholds(): assert renewals.THRESHOLDS == (30, 7, 1) and "30, 7 and 1 days ahead" in LANDING assert renewals.CERT_THRESHOLDS == (7, 1) and "with 7 days left" in LANDING and "again at 1 day" in LANDING def test_no_jargon_in_the_main_watch_copy(): main = LANDING.split("const WATCH", 1)[1].split("];", 1)[0] for word in ("MX", "DMARC", "SPF", "DKIM", "A record", "DNS"): assert word not in main, word

content.content:
- Shops are checked side by side by a small pool (`MONITOR_WORKERS=4`), each shop at its own stable minute of the
  15 minutes and of the day (a one-minute beat), never two checks of one shop at once, never two rounds stacked.
  Each check has a 150 s watchdog: one that overruns is "couldn't finish" (never passed, no alert). Python can't
  stop a thread, so the late call keeps running until its own timeout; nobody waits for it and it can't write proof.
- The daily test order records "accepted" at once and looks for "seen" in up to three later one-minute passes; still
  missing after the last one, it fails and the usual re-check / Doctor / alert path takes over.
- All GoDaddy API calls in the process share one limit (50 a minute; GoDaddy allows 60 per endpoint).
- **Public resolvers (S13b):** the daily run also asks Google 8.8.8.8, Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 and Quad9 9.9.9.9 for each
  live shop's address and saves the answers as evidence ("Reachable from 3 of 3 public resolvers"). It is information
  "Yes, I got it") under "Checked by you", apart from machine-proven hops.
- **Landing (S10.5b).** Only claims what the code does (`test_s105b_landing_claims.py` pins the numbers to
  `monitor/scheduler.py` and `renewals.py`). Sections: How it works · How the proof works (the six hops) · We keep watching
  after launch (every 15 min: opens securely; daily: the whole order path incl. a test order proving form → mail server,
  delivery proven at launch and on "Yes, I got it"; renewals 30/7/1 days, certificate 7/1; failures re-checked after a minute,
  a safe Doctor fix if allowed, one email per problem; money never spent) · Security & privacy · Check any address · Who
  it's for. A **Product menu** in the top bar (What it does · Who it's for · Free tools · Learn), a full-screen sheet on phones.
## 13. Judge Q&A

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Doesn't GoDaddy already have AI for this? | GoDaddy's AI helps people get online. LaunchWitness proves it works (a real order in her inbox) and fixes what doesn't, before customers notice. |
| Who owns the domain? | Demo: my account. Real product: her own GoDaddy account, so she owns everything. |
| What can break after launch? | Not much in a setup we control. Real risks: renewal failing, someone changing settings while connecting another tool. Monitoring is insurance. |
| If her email breaks, how do you alert her? | Personal email, not the business inbox. |
| What if she changes a setting on purpose? | Not undone silently; it asks "Was this you?" first (full monitoring). Auto-fix only when a check fails. |
| What if your server goes down? | Checks stop too. Next step: outside uptime pinger. |
| Why trust AI with money and DNS? | It can't act alone: approval, preview, backup/undo, fixed fixes, spend caps in code. |
| Where does Claude matter? | Messy price list/photo → clean profile + copy; brand-fit names; plain-words diagnosis. Code acts. |
| Why VPS not GoDaddy Hosting? | Docker VPS option runs FastAPI + many seller sites with automatic HTTPS from one box. |
| Confirm delivery for real sellers? | "Yes, I got it" link in the test email; no mailbox password [REDACTED] |
| Was the demo failure real? | Staged so it shows reliably; detection and fix are real code. |
| Cost per seller? | A few Claude calls (cents) + domain + mailbox she'd buy anyway. |
| How does she get paid? | Each order shows "Pay ₹X via UPI": a prefilled UPI link on phones and a QR on laptops, with the order ID as the note. Money goes straight from the customer's UPI app to hers; it never passes through us. She marks the order Paid after checking her UPI app. Card payments ("Connect Razorpay") come later, after the seller's KYC. |
| How does the customer know what's happening? | A status page per order (unguessable ID, first name + items only), plus a ready-typed WhatsApp message the seller sends with one tap. No SMS, no WhatsApp Business API. |
| What if she never opens her business inbox? | New orders also go to her personal email, and the customer can send the order to her WhatsApp from the thank-you screen. |
| Can a scammer launch a fake shop? | The owner's email is verified before a real launch, a policy check can hold a shop for review, every shop has "Report this shop", and the team can pause it. |
| Can a salon or tutor use it? | Not yet: v1 is for sellers who take orders. The Reader says so plainly instead of building a half-working shop. |
| Who pays renewal next year? | The seller, to GoDaddy, on her own account. We warn her at 30 / 7 / 1 days. |

---

## 14. Risks and fallbacks

| Risk | Check by | Fallback |
|---|---|---|
| Credits not yet received | Office hours Nov 14 | Build locally against OTE + fakes |
| Domain + Pro Light cost more than credit | Cart, Nov 15 | Cheaper TLD; skip Meera's domain + mailbox |
| Production Availability/DNS API blocked | Nov 15 after app domain | `gddy`, OTE or RDAP; app domain unlocks DNS |
| Mailbox creation fails via CLI/API | Nov 15 | Create in dashboard; engine still sets settings + checks delivery |
| Settings/cert slow on camera | Nov 18 rehearsal | Query authoritative NS; record the full launch |
| Claude spend creeps up | Daily | Fixtures in dev, caps on live link |
| Others build the same launch flow | — | Lead with proof + fix |
| Scope creep | Daily | No stretch before core runs end to end |
| Live demo fails at Dec 11 finale | Dec 11 | Play recording, then Q&A on live app |

content.content:
# e2e: browser flows (Playwright)

```bash
cd e2e && npm install && npx playwright install chromium
npx playwright test                                   # against the Docker stack: https://launchwitness.localhost
LW_BASE=http://localhost:8000 LW_MAIL= npx playwright test   # against the dev server (DEV_MODE=true shows links)
```

- **Docker stack** (default): start it first (`deploy/README.md`). Sign-in links are read from Mailpit
  (http://localhost:8025). The browser accepts Caddy's local CA **only for `.localhost`**.
- **Dev server**: the settings also read the repo's `.env`, so pin everything that could reach the real world
  (fixture Claude, fakes, a scratch database, SMTP to a closed port so no email can leave):

  ```bash
  cd backend && DEV_MODE=true APP_DOMAIN=localhost APP_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8000 USE_FAKES=true CLAUDE_MODE=fixture     GODADDY_ENV=ote ALLOW_PURCHASE=false ANTHROPIC_API_KEY= GODADDY_API_KEY= GODADDY_API_SECRET= MONITOR_ENABLED=false     ADMIN_EMAIL=admin@launchwitness.localhost ADMIN_TOKEN=dev-server-only-admin-token     SMTP_HOST=127.0.0.1 SMTP_PORT=9 SMTP_SECURITY=starttls SMTP_PASSWORD= [REDACTED]     DATABASE_URL=sqlite:///./data/e2e-dev.db SIGNIN_LINKS_PER_EMAIL_PER_DAY=100 SIGNIN_LINKS_PER_IP_PER_HOUR=200     VISITOR_DESCRIBES_PER_DAY=50 VISITOR_LAUNCHES_PER_DAY=50 USER_DESCRIBES_PER_DAY=50     ../.venv/Scripts/python -m uvicorn app.main:app --port 8000
  ```
- Flows: (a) sign-up → pending → team approves → describe → practice launch → real launch (pretend GoDaddy) → a
  customer order on the shop's own host → report → share link opened logged out; (b) two sellers can't reach each
  other's shop, preview, orders, export, names, plans, report or share by URL; (c) guest practice is kept after signing
  in; (d) Privacy and Terms are one click from sign-in; (e) "Start" asks to sign in first and returns to Describe, routing
  (refresh, Back/Forward, step header, Page not found) and the demo shop; (f) every link and button in the owner's preview
  stays inside the shop. Flow (a) also checks the go-live gate and the Orders page (status + WhatsApp link).
  (g) landing menu; (h) S12: staged fault + Doctor trace, symptom box, hop track, "Something breaks", photos;
  (i) S13: an order placed while the team's practice "mail down" switch is on shows "Email to you: retrying" and becomes
  "sent" after it's off; sign-in while the mail server is unreachable says "We're having trouble sending email" and the
  link still arrives. The sign-in flow runs `docker stop/start launchwitness-local-mailpit-1` (`LW_MAILPIT_CONTAINER`
  to rename), so it only runs on the local Docker stack and is skipped elsewhere.
- Screenshots (not a test): `npx playwright test -c screens.config.ts` → `docs/screenshots/s10-5/` (`LW_SHOTS=<dir>`).
- Not covered here: the owner tapping "Yes, I got it". On a practice server the test-order email goes to the
  pretend inbox (in server memory), so there's no link to tap; pytest covers that path

"""Team tool (S19B): run one round of checks for a shop from the command line, inside the app container, through the
same code the app uses. Prints results, the test email's SUBJECT only (never addresses, bodies or secrets), the
shared-report count and whether the proof chain is intact. Every run is audited (actor "admin (cli)").

    docker compose ... exec -T app python /app/scripts/admin_check_shop.py <subdomain> manual|daily

manual = what "Run checks now" does (test email to the shop's order address, with "Yes, I got it").
daily  = one daily monitoring round (test email to LaunchWitness's check mailbox), plus the later inbox passes.
"""

import json
import sys
import time

from sqlmodel import Session, select

from app import audit, chain, proof
from app.agents.launch_check import latest_launched_plan, run_checks
from app.config import get_settings
from app.db import get_engine
from app.integrations import for_business, get_integrations, get_practice_integrations
from app.models import Business, CheckResult, CheckRun, Order, Outbox, TestTicket
from app.routers.businesses import get_claude
from app.routers.report import run_out
from app.sites.orders import TEST_BANNER


def main(subdomain: str, kind: str) -> int:
    settings, engine = get_settings(), get_engine()
    server, practice = get_integrations(), get_practice_integrations()
    integ_for = lambda b: for_business(b, server, practice)  # noqa: E731
    claude = get_claude(settings)
    with Session(engine) as s:
        b = s.exec(select(Business).where(Business.subdomain == subdomain)).first()
        if b is None:
            print("no such shop")
            return 2
        plan = latest_launched_plan(s, b.id)
        audit.record(s, actor="admin (cli)", action="run_checks_now" if kind == "manual" else "monitor_daily_now",
                     target=plan.site_host, result="ok", business_id=b.id, detail="scripts/admin_check_shop.py")
        bid, plan_id = b.id, plan.id
    if kind == "manual":
        summary = run_checks(engine, settings, integ_for(b), claude, plan_id, trigger="manual")
        run_id = summary.run_id
    else:
        from app.monitor.scheduler import Monitor

        mon = Monitor(engine, settings, integ_for, claude)
        mon.check_business(bid, "daily")
        jobs = [j for j in mon.scheduler.get_jobs() if j.id.startswith("inbox-")]
        for job in jobs:  # the later inbox passes the running scheduler would do, one minute apart
            _b, run_id, item, n = job.args
            while True:
                time.sleep(60)
                got = mon.inbox_pass(bid, run_id, item, n)
                print("inbox pass", n, got)
                if got != "later":
                    break
                n += 1
        with Session(engine) as s:
            run_id = s.exec(select(CheckRun.id).where(CheckRun.business_id == bid, CheckRun.trigger == "monitor_daily")
                            .order_by(CheckRun.id.desc())).first()
    with Session(engine) as s:
        run = s.get(CheckRun, run_id)
        out = run_out(s, run)
        proof.summary(s, out)
        print(f"run {run.id} trigger={run.trigger} passed={run.passed}")
        for c in out["checks"]:
            print(f"  {c['check']:<12} {c.get('state', ''):<10} {c['title']}  | {c['plain'][:110]}")
            if c["check"] == "test_order":
                print("     hops:", " -> ".join(h["title"] for h in c["hops"]))
        t = s.exec(select(TestTicket).where(TestTicket.run_id == run.id)).first()
        if t and t.order_id:
            o = s.get(Order, t.order_id)
            row = s.exec(select(Outbox).where(Outbox.key == f"order:{o.id}")).first()
            app_box = settings.smtp_user.lower()
            print(f"  test ticket audience={t.audience or 'order address'} confirm_link={'yes' if t.confirm_hash else 'no'}")
            print(f"  test email to the check mailbox: {app_box in row.to_addr.lower()}; recipients: "
                  f"{len([a for a in row.to_addr.split(',') if a.strip()])}")
            found = server.inbox.find(subject_contains=t.nonce, since=t.created_at.replace(tzinfo=None)
                                      if False else None) if not server.fake else []
            for m in found[:1]:
                print(f"  IMAP subject: {m.subject}")
                print(f"  body opens with the TEST banner: {m.body.lstrip().startswith(TEST_BANNER)}; "
                      f"no customer links: {'wa.me' not in m.body and 'tel:' not in m.body}")
        from app.models import ShareLink  # noqa: F401  (only to fail loudly if the model is renamed)
        print("  chain:", json.dumps(chain.verify(s, bid))[:200])
        latest = s.exec(select(CheckResult).where(CheckResult.business_id == bid).order_by(CheckResult.id.desc())).first()
        print("  latest result row:", latest.check if latest else None)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "manual"))

# Build log — how LaunchWitness was built with Claude Code

One entry per Claude Code session, newest last. This is what judges read to understand the process; the full transcripts are in the combined replay at `/build`.

## Template (copy for each session)

```
### Session N — YYYY-MM-DD — <short title>
- Goal: <milestone + acceptance criteria targeted>
- Asked Claude to: <1–2 lines>
- Claude built: <files/features>
- I changed / rejected: <what the human decided or corrected>
- Result: <ACs passed, tests, what works now>
- Next: <one line>
```

---

### Session 0 — 2026-11-14 — Ideation and spec
- Goal: settle the idea and plan before writing code.
- Worked with Claude (chat) to pressure-test the idea: dropped "rollback after launch" as the hero after realizing that in a setup we control, little breaks post-launch; moved repair into the launch itself; kept light monitoring.
- Output: `docs/SPEC.md`, `docs/BUILD_PLAN.md`, `CLAUDE.md`.
- Next: M0 scaffold.

### Session 1 — 2026-11-14 — M0 scaffold (local, no external calls)
- Goal: M0, all three ACs (compose serves page + health ok; pytest incl. purchase-blocked and tls-ask tests; no real network in tests, no secrets).
- Asked Claude to: read the docs, propose a file-by-file plan mapped to ACs, then build M0 with every external service behind a wrapper with a fake.
- Claude built: FastAPI backend (`config`, `db`, six SQLModel tables, `audit` helper, `/api/health`, `/internal/tls-ask`); wrappers + fakes for GoDaddy (ote|prod), Claude (fixture|live), SMTP, IMAP, DNS; spend guard; 3 Indian seller fixtures (home cakes, tiffin, tailor) + a placeholder Reader fixture; Vite/React/TS health page; Dockerfile, compose, local + prod Caddyfiles; an autouse pytest guard that blocks and records any non-local network call.
- I changed / rejected: approved the plan as proposed. Notable fixes during the session: the network guard first let traffic escape via the sandbox's local HTTPS proxy (fixed by clearing proxy env vars in tests); dnspython swallows the guard's error, so that test asserts on the guard's record instead; one commit had gone in with a failing test hidden by a pipe and was amended before pushing.
- Result: 52 tests pass; stack verified at http://localhost through Caddy (health ok, `/internal/*` blocked); both Caddyfiles validate. In the cloud sandbox the image needed a scratch-only CA build secret; repo Dockerfile unchanged.
### Session 17 — 2026-11-19 — Logo, branded email, the first real shop launch, backups, deploy key (Opus, laptop)
- Goal: brand the app, deploy, launch the demo shop for real on GoDaddy DNS and prove it end to end; backups and a deploy key.
- Asked Claude to: make a transparent logo master and every icon, wire them into the app (not the shops), one copy change, one shared
  branded email layout, deploy, then watch the real launch step by step with evidence, check the proof chain, set up backups and a
  read-only deploy key.
- Claude built: `scripts/make_brand_assets.py` + `frontend/public/` icons + the header mark; `app/mail/layout.py` for every email; brand
  files served on the app host only; tests `test_s17_brand.py`, `test_s17_email_layout.py`, `test_s17_inbox_wait.py`.
- What the live run caught: the launch's inbox step called the unbuilt GoDaddy mailbox stub (fixed: sign in to our own inbox); GoDaddy's
  VPS resolvers answer some names wrongly (the app container now uses public DNS); my email layout made the IMAP body empty (fixed); the
  mailbox search index lags, so a test order could miss a 40 s window (now 120 s with a header scan, and the report says it's waiting).
- I changed / rejected: the logo isn't purple, so its real lime/ink colours were kept (lime button, not purple); DNS change on the app
  container only; asked for the longer wait + header scan; the restore test goes into a temp folder, not over the local stack.
- Result: shop live with a real certificate, 7/7 checks, the shared report verifies (intact); backend 1355 passed; secret scan clean.
- Next: demo video, README, brief PDF, submission.
